meta.scope: South Korea Batch 4 — Additional structural surveys (Business Activities, Service Industry, National Business Survey), regional depth (GRDP / regional accounts), housing / real-estate statistics, and remaining high-value uniqueness nodes. Continues under locked definition.
meta.strategy_note: Fills remaining structural and regional gaps after Batches 1–3. Emphasises services (large share of economy), business-structure data relevant to chaebol/SME analysis, spatial concentration via GRDP, and housing (a major social and financial issue in Korea).

candidates.title: Survey of Business Activities (기업활동조사)
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT) / Ministry of Data and Statistics
candidates.description: Annual survey of corporations (primarily those above size thresholds) covering business results, diversification, affiliated companies, tangible/intangible assets, domestic and overseas transactions, and management direction. Provides structural insight into larger firms and business groups.
candidates.notes: Complements the BOK Financial Statement Analysis with broader business-activity and affiliation data. Useful for analysing diversification, group structures and the behaviour of large enterprises that dominate Korea’s export and industrial landscape.

candidates.title: Service Industry Survey / Monthly Service Industry Survey
candidates.description: Annual structural survey and monthly short-term survey of service-industry establishments covering sales, employment and related indicators across wholesale/retail, accommodation/food, information/communication, real estate, professional services, education, health and other service sectors.
candidates.notes: Essential for a services-heavy modern economy. The monthly series provides timely activity indicators that complement industrial production; the annual survey supplies structural detail. Parallel to Japan’s Tertiary Industry Activity and related service surveys.

candidates.title: National Business Survey / Census of Establishments (전국사업체조사)
candidates.description: Periodic comprehensive survey of business establishments (all or large sample) providing counts of establishments and workers by industry, size, region and organisational form. Benchmark for business demography and sampling frames.
candidates.notes: Structural foundation for understanding the distribution of economic activity across firm sizes and regions. Complements the Economic Census-style products and feeds into national accounts and industrial statistics.

candidates.title: Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP) / Regional Accounts
candidates.region: Republic of Korea (by province / metropolitan city)
candidates.description: Annual (and experimental quarterly) estimates of gross regional domestic product by province and metropolitan city, with industry breakdowns. Quantifies the extreme concentration of economic activity in the Seoul Capital Area (Seoul + Gyeonggi + Incheon) versus other regions.
candidates.notes: Core regional-contrast series. Seoul Capital Area typically accounts for roughly half of national GDP; GRDP data make the hierarchy and peripheral-region differentials explicit. Parallel to Japan’s Prefectural Accounts + Tokyo/Okinawa contrast.

candidates.title: Housing statistics and House Price / Transaction indices
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea / Korea Real Estate Board (REB) / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on housing stock, ownership, household housing conditions, and price/transaction indices for apartments and other dwellings (including actual-transaction price indices). Housing is a central social and financial issue in Korea.
candidates.notes: High-value uniqueness node. Housing prices, ownership concentration and household debt linked to housing are major policy and social concerns. Complements the Survey of Household Finances and Living Conditions and regional accounts.

candidates.title: Construction statistics / Construction orders and permits
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea / Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport
candidates.description: Statistics on construction orders, building permits, housing starts and related construction-activity indicators. Important short-term and structural series for investment and housing-supply analysis.
candidates.notes: Links industrial production, fixed investment in the national accounts, and housing-market statistics. Useful for understanding the construction cycle and housing-supply responses.

candidates.title: SME / Small and Medium Enterprise statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of SMEs and Startups / Statistics Korea / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on the number, employment, sales and financial conditions of small and medium-sized enterprises, often contrasted with large enterprises. Complements the large-firm focus of the Financial Statement Analysis and Survey of Business Activities.
candidates.notes: Balances the chaebol / large-enterprise picture with the SME sector that employs the majority of workers. Relevant to industrial-policy and regional-economy analysis.

candidates.title: R&D and innovation statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Science and ICT / Statistics Korea / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on research and development expenditure, personnel, patents and innovation activities by sector and firm size. Reflects Korea’s high R&D intensity and technology-driven growth model.
candidates.notes: High-value uniqueness node. Korea’s R&D-to-GDP ratio is among the world’s highest; these series link education, industrial structure and export competitiveness (especially semiconductors and ICT).

candidates.title: ICT / Digital economy statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Science and ICT / Statistics Korea / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on ICT industry production, employment, broadband/internet penetration, digital trade and related digital-economy indicators.
candidates.notes: Complements R&D and industrial-production series. Korea’s advanced digital infrastructure and ICT export strength are distinctive features of its economic structure.

candidates.title: Extended regional contrast (Seoul Capital Area vs non-capital provinces / GRDP + demographic differentials)
candidates.description: Synthesised framework that systematically compares the Seoul Capital Area with other provinces and metropolitan cities using GRDP, population, ageing, fertility, employment and housing indicators. Tests hierarchy homogeneity and surfaces core–periphery differentials.
referenced_by: Population Census and Vital Statistics regional tables
Housing and labour statistics by province
candidates.notes: Meta-node that operationalises the regional-contrast principle for Korea. Extreme concentration in the Seoul Capital Area is a defining structural feature; explicit comparison with peripheral provinces (e.g., Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Gangwon, Jeju) strengthens the graph’s ability to capture spatial inequality and policy responses.
